g.text: Airsoft reaction targets - hardware overview - sheet 1/3 - rev 2.0.1 - 2026-10-24
AIRSOFT REACTION TARGETS - hardware v2 (as built)
One hub and up to 5 identical targets. The boards are not wired together: the targets talk to the
hub over ESP-NOW (WiFi channel 1 by default). Phones join the hub's WiFi and open the app.
Double-click a sheet to open it.
Target node (one per target, up to 5) - sheet 2/3 - rev 2.0.1 - 2026-10-24
TARGET NODE - one per target, up to 5, all identical (same firmware)
As built: WeMos D1 Mini + battery shield (stacked) + SW-420 + one WS2812B. No wires to the hub: ESP-NOW radio.
Shield J2 closed: BAT+ -> 130k -> A0. The D1 Mini has its own 220k/100k divider on A0,
so the ADC sees Vbat x 100/450 (1.0 V full scale = 4.5 V, ~4.4 mV per count).
Firmware default batt_scale_uv = 4102 assumes 4.2 V full scale: calibrate each target
once in the app (Targets > target > Battery calibration) with a multimeter reading.
SW1 (optional): with it off the cell is disconnected, so the shield cannot charge it.
Free pins: D0, D5, D6, D7, D8 (and D2 when JP1 is bridged to A).
D4/GPIO2 = on-board LED and boot pin. TX/RX = USB serial console.
The 3V3 pin is the D1 Mini regulator output (feeds the SW-420).
Power from 3V3 so DO is 3.3 V logic. Rising edge = hit (interrupt on GPIO5).
Coarse sensitivity: the module pot. Fine: lockout and pulses in the app.
JP1 A = D3/GPIO0 (current targets). JP1 B = D2/GPIO4 (recommended for new
targets; set "LED pin" for that target in the app). GPIO0 is a boot pin: if the
LED holds it low at power-up, the board starts in flash mode.
WS2812B on 5 V with 3.3 V data is marginal (needs 0.7 x VDD) but works for one
LED. If it flickers, power the LED from 3V3 instead.
R1 330R and C1 100uF: recommended, not fitted on every target.
Runs the games, the WiFi AP "Airsoft-Master" (app at http://192.168.4.1) and ESP-NOW to the targets.
Micro-USB: USB power bank or charger (about 0.5 W).
Nothing else is wired. No PSRAM, 4 MB flash.
Avoid GPIO0, 2, 12, 15 (boot straps) and GPIO1/3 (USB serial).
Pin numbers follow the 30-pin DOIT DevKit V1. 38-pin boards have
the same GPIOs in a different header order: wire by GPIO name.
